text.p: South African mining group Gencor Ltd said on Monday it expected its base metal division Billiton to be floated in the range of 210 to 240 pence a share on the London Stock Exchange.

Billiton is expected to issue about 375 million new shares, giving it a market capitalisation of between 4.4 billion and 5.1 billion pounds, Gencor said in its prospectus. It estimated Billiton's attributable profit excluding exceptional items was at least $330 million in the year ended June 30, and published a pro forma dividend of 10 cents.
The expected profits give Billiton a proforma earnings per share of 19.3 cents (12 pence).
Conditional dealings in Billiton's shares are expected to commence on the London market on July 23.
Post listing, Billiton will become the second mining group in the FTSE 100, joining Rio Tinto Plc which has a market capitalisation of 22 billion pounds ($37.2 billion).
Gencor said roadshow presentations to institutional investors in connection with the proposed flotation would begin on Monday.
The money raised from the float will be used to finance Billiton's future exploration and other green-field development projects. ($ = 0.591 British Pounds).
